Description

Boulder County Public Health is seeking to hire an Environmental Health Specialist.
This position works in the Food Safety Program and performs a variety of duties to help prevent the spread of disease, mitigate health risks, and ensure compliance with all food safety rules and regulations. This position may be filled at either the Environmental Health Specialist I (EH I) or Environmental Health Specialist II (EH II) level, depending upon qualifications and experience.

Environmental Health Specialist II: Conducts inspections and investigations with greater proficiency and broader responsibility. Documents violations, recommend enforcement actions, participate in specialized teams, independently implement program requirements, trains staff, contribute to special projects, and may assume limited supervisory responsibilities as needed.

Environmental Health Specialist I: Performs basic to intermediate environmental health inspections and investigations in accordance with Colorado and Boulder County regulations. Training is provided for inspections, complaint investigations, permitting, plan review, and other program responsibilities. Documents violations and recommends enforcement actions to a supervisor.

This is a full-time, benefited position
that will work Monday- Friday: 8:00am- 4:30pm.
This position will work at 3450 Broadway Street in Boulder,
CO. Under Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA) guidelines, this position is exempt.

Boulder County requires its employees to reside in the state of Colorado as of the first day of work.

Hiring Salary Range:
EH2 $70,428.00-$85,908.00

EH1 $60,840.00-$74,178.00

Tentative Hiring Timeline

Phone Screening: Week of November 16th
First Round Interviews: Week of November 16th
Second Round Interviews: Week of November 23rd
Reference Check: Week of November 23rd

New employees receive an80-hour bank (Download PDF reader) of vacation at the time of hire, in addition to 8 hours of both vacation and medical leave accruals each month (Must not have been employed at Boulder County during the 12 months prior to re-hire date to qualify).Boulder County offers bountiful benefits, including pension contributions.

Boulder County employees may qualify for Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF). Visit studentaid.gov for more information.

Examples of Duties

Enforces federal, state, and local regulations and ordinances related to assigned areas.
Conducts routine inspections; issues permits and licenses where appropriate.
Performs complaint investigations and other environmental health investigations.
Performs plan review of newly constructed and remodeled retail food establishments.
Maintains electronic records and databases and prepares reports and documentation.
Responds to foodborne illness and other public health incidents.
Develops and conducts educational classes and presentations.
Performs other duties as assigned and may be reassigned in emergency situations.

Required Qualifications

PLEASE NOTE: When completing your application describe all relevant education and experience, as applications are assessed based on the required qualifications listed. Resumes and other attachments are not accepted in lieu of completed applications and will not be reviewed in the initial screening process. Any personally identifiable information (PII) such as name and address will be redacted from applications that meet the minimum screening requirements and are forwarded to the hiring manager. If the hiring manager selects you to advance in the hiring process, your attachments will then be shared with the hiring team.

Education & Experience

Boulder County is looking for well qualified candidates to fill our positions. Any combination of relevant education and experience is encouraged. In this position, we are looking for a minimum of

Environmental Health Specialist II

Six years performing technical tasks in investigation of environmental health conditions, or
A bachelor's degree in physical, biological, or sanitary sciences or related field plus two years performing technical tasks in investigation of environmental health conditions, or

Any equivalent combination of experience and education

Environmental Health Specialist I

Four years of professional experience in a related program, or
A bachelor's degree in physical, biological, or sanitary sciences or related field, or

Any equivalent combination of experience and education

Driver's License

Applicants must have a valid driver's license, a good driving record, and current automobile insurance
Must have a valid driver’s license in good standing; adequate automobile insurance; and access to reliable transportation that is readily available for business use

Background Check

A job offer is contingent on passing a background investigation

Supplemental Information

Knowledge, Skills And Abilities

Ability to independently conduct inspections, review plans, issue permits, and apply regulations to assigned programmatic areas.
Ability to lead complaint investigations with minimal input and oversight from supervisor.
Ability to document violations and recommend enforcement actions.
Ability to implement program requirements independently.
Ability to demonstrate competency in data entry, database management, report writing, permit documentation, and inspection records.

Preferred Qualificaitons

Knowledge of educational and community outreach strategies.
Ability to understand, interpret, and apply statutes and regulations pertaining to food safety.
Ability to conduct educational classes effectively.
Excellent collaboration skills, with the ability to establish and maintain strong and effective working relationships with coworkers, partners, clients, outside agencies, and the public.
Excellent written and oral communication skills.
Knowledge of modern practices, procedures, and methods of environmental health and sanitation as related to food safety.
Ability to perform moderately complex problem-solving operations.
Ability to keep accurate records.
Proficiency in databases
Proficiency in Microsoft Office (e.g. Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook); GIS experience is preferred.

jobs.title: Hazardous Materials Specialist
jobs.description:
What's The Role And What You'll Do

See the risk. Find the solution. Protect the community.

A chemical inventory tells you what a business stores. A site inspection tells you a bigger story.

Are incompatible materials stored together? Does the emergency plan reflect what is actually happening on site? Would first responders have the information they need when it matters most?

If those are the questions that get your attention, bring your curiosity, technical knowledge, and practical judgment to the City of Mountain View.

As our Hazardous Materials Specialist
, you’ll help businesses operate safely, support firefighters with technical expertise, and protect the people and places that make up our community. Reporting to the Fire Marshal in the Fire and Environmental Protection Division, you’ll connect science, fieldwork, education, and enforcement with opportunities to see the direct impact of your work.

Picture your workday

Your morning might begin with reviewing hazardous materials business plans in the California Environmental Reporting System (CERS) for the sites that will be inspected. This includes familiarizing yourself with the site and their prior inspection history.

Later, you head into the field. An inspection gives you the chance to compare the paperwork with actual conditions, evaluate potential hazards, and explain corrective actions in clear, practical terms.

Back at the office, you could review construction plans, document inspection findings, or coordinate with another agency on a regulatory question. When a hazardous materials emergency occurs, you may be called on to provide technical guidance to the Incident Commander.

Across these assignments, your judgment matters and so does your ability to help people understand and act on it.

Real work. Visible impact.

Your Assignments Will Connect You With Work Such As

Safer business operations: Review hazardous materials business plans, process permits, and help facilities understand and meet applicable requirements.
Underground storage tank oversight: Inspect monitoring systems, installations, and removals to evaluate compliance.
Construction and facility changes: Review proposed construction and hazardous materials facility closure plans for compliance with applicable requirements.
Field inspections and follow-through: Investigate concerns, document findings, explain necessary corrections, and take enforcement action when needed.
Emergency readiness and response: Educate firefighters, City employees, and industry safety personnel, and provide technical expertise during hazardous materials incidents.

The Essentials

Bring your science. Bring your people skills.

You can recognize a chemical hazard and explain why it matters to someone without your technical background. You ask thoughtful questions, write clear reports, and remain steady when circumstances change.

You understand that effective compliance takes both professional relationships and consistent follow-through. You’re comfortable helping someone work through a complicated requirement, and you can be firm when a condition needs to be corrected.

Relevant experience may come from hazardous materials compliance, environmental consulting, laboratory or industrial chemical safety, or other work involving hazardous materials storage and handling. Tell us how your background prepares you for this role.

Why bring your expertise to Mountain View? Help make innovation safe.

Mountain View is a place where people come to develop ideas, build businesses, and shape what comes next. As our Hazardous Materials Specialist, you’ll help create the conditions for that work to happen safely—with attention to the people handling hazardous materials, the firefighters responding to emergencies, and the community around them.

Here, your expertise reaches across the life of a facility: from reviewing proposed construction and hazardous materials business plans to conducting inspections, guiding corrective actions, and reviewing closure plans. You’ll have opportunities to understand how a business operates, identify what needs to change, and help turn a technical requirement into a practical solution.

You’ll also bring that knowledge directly into the Fire Department. Reporting to the Fire Marshal, you’ll support prevention efforts, help prepare first responders, and provide technical guidance during hazardous materials emergencies.

For someone who enjoys science, fieldwork, and working with people, that combination offers a compelling opportunity: build your expertise while seeing how your decisions help protect a whole community.

View the full job description here: Hazardous Materials Specialist

Are We a Match?

What You’ll Need

The classification calls for education equivalent to a bachelor’s degree in chemistry, biology, fire science/fire technology, or an environmentally related field, plus two years of recent full-time experience dealing with the storage and/or handling of hazardous materials. A combination of relevant experience, education, and training that satisfies the required qualifications will be considered.

Education, experience, and knowledge involving local, State, or Federal hazardous materials and fire prevention codes and regulations are also required.

You’ll need a valid California driver license upon appointment. Within six months of appointment, you must complete California Peace Officer Standards and Training PC 832 training and obtain ICC California Underground Storage Tank Inspector certification.

This position includes enforcement activities and response to hazardous materials emergencies. Work may involve strenuous physical effort, unpleasant environments, and potentially significant and unpredictable hazards.

Compensation

Full range $167,726 to $226,924 annually, with a control point of $197,325. Starting salary is flexible within the range based on experience, specialized expertise, and internal equity. The anticipated hiring range for this position is $167,726 to $197,325; i nitial salary placement will be based on the selected candidate’s qualifications, relevant experience, and alignment with the position.

Apply Now

Put Your Expertise To Work For a Whole Community.

If you enjoy connecting technical details to practical solutions and want your work to help keep businesses, first responders, and the public safe we invite you to bring that perspective to Mountain View.

Application and Selection

Apply online through GovernmentJobs.com before November
20, 2026; 5 PM
. Applications must be complete and received by the deadline.

Anticipated Date for Virtual Oral Boards:
Mid January 2027

Anticipated Date for In-Person Interviews:
Late January 2027

Anticipated Hire Date:
Early March 2027

Accessibility and Accommodations

The City of Mountain View is committed to providing an accessible and inclusive recruitment process. If you need a reasonable accommodation to complete the application or participate in any stage of the selection process, please contact Human Resources at (650) 903-6309. Advance notice helps us make timely arrangements, but accommodation requests may be made at any stage of the process.

If you are unable to apply online, please contact the City of Mountain View Human Resources Department at (650) 903-6309 or visit the City’s Application Information webpage for assistance or an alternative application method.

Equal Employment Opportunity

The City of Mountain View is an equal opportunity employer. Applicants are considered based on job-related qualifications without regard to any status protected by federal, state, or local law.
